questions.q: Which question does Controlling (CO) answer that financial accounting (FI) alone does not?
options: Who spent the money, for which purpose, and what it earned
How much the insurer owes Skattestyrelsen
What the legal balance sheet looks like
Which bank account received a premium
questions.reason: FI is the legal view of what was spent; CO is the internal management view of who spent it and why.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, where do FI and CO postings land?
options: In one shared table, the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)
In separate FI and CO tables reconciled every night
Only in the CO table; FI reads a copy
In a spreadsheet uploaded at month-end
questions.reason: FI and CO share the Universal Journal, so every cost line carries both the GL account and a cost object.

questions.q: Why do FI and CO totals agree by design in S/4HANA?
options: Both read the same lines in ACDOCA
A batch job copies FI totals into CO every hour
Auditors adjust CO to match FI
questions.reason: There is only one journal line per posting, read by both FI and CO, so no separate reconciliation is needed.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, what is a cost element?
options: A GL account (FS00) with a cost element category
A separate master record created only in CO
A budget on an internal order
questions.reason: Cost elements are GL accounts; the category says whether it is primary or secondary and how CO may use it.

questions.q: Which of these is a primary cost element in the lesson?
questions.reason: Rent is a real cost from outside the company posted in FI. 940000 is secondary, and bank and reserves are balance sheet accounts.

questions.q: What is special about a secondary cost element such as 940000?
options: It only moves costs inside CO; no money leaves the company
It is used to pay suppliers
It is a balance sheet account
questions.reason: Secondary cost elements are used for allocations and settlements between cost objects, so FI profit does not change.

questions.q: What is a cost centre?
options: A place in the company where costs arise and someone is responsible for them, usually a department
A policyholder who makes many claims
A temporary campaign with an end date
questions.reason: Cost centres are permanent and have a manager. Temporary jobs use internal orders instead.

questions.q: Which transaction creates a cost centre such as 4100 IT?
questions.reason: KS01 creates cost centres. KO01 creates internal orders, KSU5 runs assessments and KE30 runs profitability reports.

questions.q: What is the standard hierarchy?
options: The one tree in the controlling area (NF00) that every cost centre must belong to
A list of GL accounts in the chart of accounts
The approval chain for supplier invoices
The order in which month-end jobs run
questions.reason: Every cost centre hangs in the standard hierarchy, whose groups make reporting on several cost centres easy.

questions.q: Why does an insurer split operating costs into claims handling, acquisition and administration?
options: The combined ratio and the statutory and IFRS 17 reporting need the types separately
Because SAP cannot post costs without three types
Because every cost centre must have exactly three accounts
questions.reason: Reporting needs the split. The exact rules should be confirmed with the finance and actuarial teams.

questions.q: Which cost at Nordica is an acquisition cost?
questions.reason: Acquisition costs are the cost of winning policies, such as advertising and sales. Telephony for claims is claims handling and rent is administration.

questions.q: On 01.03 the March rent of DKK 50,000 is posted. Which line carries cost centre 3000?
options: Neither line; CO adds it later
questions.reason: Only the expense line (a primary cost element) needs a cost object. The bank line is a balance sheet account.

questions.q: Which report shows every actual posting on a cost centre, line by line?
questions.reason: KSB1 lists cost centre actual line items. KE5Z is for profit centre line items.

questions.q: Telephony on cost centre 1000 was planned at DKK 16,000 and the actual is DKK 18,000. What is the variance?
questions.reason: Variance is actual minus plan: 18,000 − 16,000 = 2,000 over plan.

questions.q: Which report compares plan and actual per cost centre?
questions.reason: S_ALR_87013611 is the cost centres actual/plan/variance report. The others are AR line items, goods movements and the payment run.

questions.q: When should you use an internal order instead of a cost centre?
options: For a temporary campaign or project whose total cost you want to see on its own
questions.reason: Internal orders are short-lived cost collectors with a budget and an end date, like order 700100 for the spring motor campaign.

questions.q: Order 700100 has online ads 40,000, agency 10,000 and events 15,000. Budget is 80,000. How much budget is left?
What happens when order 700100 is settled with KO88?
options: The order is credited and cost centre 2000 Sales and distribution is debited with DKK 65,000
questions.reason: Settlement empties the order to the receiver in its settlement rule, leaving the order balance at 0.

questions.q: IT costs of DKK 24,000 are assessed by headcount: Claims handling 30, Sales 10, Administration 8. How much does Claims handling receive?
questions.reason: 24,000 × 30/48 = 15,000. Sales gets 5,000 and Administration 4,000, together 24,000.

questions.q: After the March IT assessment, what is the balance on cost centre 4100 IT?
questions.reason: The sender is credited with the full 24,000 it shared out, so 24,000 − 24,000 = 0.

questions.q: Which pair of transactions creates and runs an assessment cycle?
options: KSU1 to create, KSU5 to run
KO01 to create, KO88 to run
KS01 to create, KSB1 to run
KE30 to create, KE5Z to run
questions.reason: KSU1 defines the cycle (sender, receivers, key, secondary cost element) and KSU5 executes it, ideally as a test run first.

questions.q: What is the main difference between an assessment and a distribution?
options: Assessment uses a secondary cost element; distribution keeps the original primary cost element
Assessment moves money to the bank; distribution does not
questions.reason: In an assessment the receiver sees '940000 IT assessment'; in a distribution it sees the original cost type.

questions.q: What is a profit centre in the insurance example?
options: A line of business such as PC-MOTOR or PC-HOME, run like a small company with its own result
A department that only has costs
questions.reason: Profit centres collect premium, claims and costs per line of business so management can see the result of each.

questions.q: Motor has earned premium 1,000,000 and claims incurred 700,000. What is its loss ratio?
questions.reason: Loss ratio = claims incurred ÷ earned premium = 700,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 70%.

questions.q: Home has earned premium 600,000 and operating expenses 150,000. What is its expense ratio?
questions.reason: Expense ratio = operating expenses ÷ earned premium = 150,000 ÷ 600,000 = 25%.

questions.q: What is the combined ratio?
options: Loss ratio plus expense ratio: (claims incurred + operating expenses) ÷ earned premium
Gross written premium divided by claims paid
Earned premium divided by unearned premium
questions.reason: The combined ratio adds the loss ratio and the expense ratio. Home: 60% + 25% = 85%.

questions.q: What does a combined ratio below 100% mean?
options: The insurance business itself earns an underwriting profit
The insurer makes an underwriting loss
The premium has not been earned yet
questions.reason: Below 100% means premium earned is more than claims and costs. Motor at 90% keeps 10 øre of every krone.

questions.q: What is the combined ratio for the whole company in March (earned premium 1,600,000, claims incurred 1,060,000, operating expenses 350,000)?
questions.reason: (1,060,000 + 350,000) ÷ 1,600,000 = 88.125%, which is the loss ratio 66.25% plus the expense ratio 21.875%.

questions.q: How is earned premium calculated?
options: Gross written premium minus the change in the unearned premium reserve
Claims paid plus the change in claims reserves
Gross written premium plus insurance tax
questions.reason: Motor: 1,500,000 − 500,000 = 1,000,000. Earned premium is the part of the premium that belongs to the months already passed.

questions.q: Which transaction runs a profitability report by line of business, product, channel or region?
questions.reason: KE30 runs profitability (margin analysis) reports. KSB1 is cost centre line items, KO01 creates orders and OKP1 locks CO periods.

questions.q: At month-end, why are orders settled and cycles run before plan/actual and margin reports?
options: So the reports show costs on the departments and lines that finally carry them
The order does not matter at all
questions.reason: Senders must be complete and shared out first; otherwise the reports show IT and the campaign costs in the wrong place.

questions.q: A manager says the numbers on her cost centre are wrong. What is a good first step?
options: Open KSB1 and follow one line item: account, cost centre, and whether it was moved by settlement or assessment
Delete the cost centre and create a new one
Ask IT to rebuild the report
Post a correction in FI without checking
questions.reason: Most 'wrong numbers' come from a missing or wrong cost object, which line items show quickly.
